newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close higher on Wall Street gain.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close higher on Wall Street gain.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Sunday in response to the rise of U.S. stocks on Friday, but the gains were weighed down later in the day by profit taking, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 1.53 percent, or 3.66 points, to 242.79 on high all-share turnover of 194 million shekels against 150 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.31 percent higher at 251.38.

"The session opened with nice gains and the indices rose by more than 2.25 percent. By midday the market weakened slightly as investors started taking profits," said Shahar Gazit of Batucha Securities and Investments.
"The rise of American stocks and Israeli shares traded in New York had a positive impact on trading despite the fact that the market is not looking for reasons to rise," Gazit said.

"The market is continuing to rise very quickly but a technical correction has to come," said Elisha Rosenfeld of Lehava Investments. "The fact that new money keeps coming into the market prevents it from completing such a correction."

Industrial Buildings, the main gainer on the Maof, surged the maximum 10 percent to 512 agorot. UBS Ltd issued a "buy" recommendation for the company, saying the share was trading sharply below its underlying asset value.

Makhteshim Chemical Works rose 2.75 percent to 1,711 agorot. A source close to the company said on Sunday that Makhteshim had signed a pact with Germany's Bayer AG giving Makhteshim exclusive rights to a Bayer agricultural herbicide.

The most active shares were Bank Leumi, which gained 2.0 percent to 525 agorot on volume of 11.2 million shekels, and Bank Hapoalim, which rose 1.5 percent to 615 agorot on turnover of 10 million shekels.

Teva Pharmaceutical Industries rose 5.0 percent to 1,812 agorot. Teva's American depositary receipts, which are traded on Nasdaq, rose 7.6 percent during the last two days of the U.S. trading week on hopes for improved results for the last quarter of 1996, analysts said.
